bibliography.abstract: We describe the solver we submitted to the second round of the SOICT 2026 contest on the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation problem, a selective pickup-and-delivery routing problem with time windows, open routes and heterogeneous taxis. The solver is a single-file, standard-library Python program that combines (i) a constant-time insertion test based on latest-arrival slack, (ii) greedy insertion, local search and an Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS) with simulated-annealing acceptance, and (iii) an exact route-selection engine that enumerates, for every taxi, the best feasible route for each request set and then solves the resulting set-packing problem by branch-and-bound strengthened with route-based large neighborhood search, Lagrangian bounds and reduced-cost fixing. The engine is chosen automatically from the instance size, and an independent verifier and a watchdog guarantee that a valid answer is always printed. On the official evaluation (38 scored instances, 5-minute limit) the solver obtained a total benefit of 487,237, finished every run within 277 s and used at most 279 MB; 28 of the 38 instances terminated well before the limit.
bibliography.comment: 5 pages, 1 figure, 2 tables. Technical Report for the SOICT 2026 Student Contest. Code: https://github.com/25023189-bit/Integrated-Passenger-and-Parcel-Transportation-SOICT-2026
bibliography.title: A Hybrid Exact-Heuristic Solver for the Integrated Passenger and Parcel Transportation Problem

en.what: A single-file Python solver combines local search heuristics—including Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search and constant-time insertion tests—with an exact branch-and-bound set-packing engine for integrated passenger and parcel transport. Evaluated on 38 official competition instances with a 5-minute time limit, the algorithm achieved a total benefit of 487,237 while utilizing less than 279 MB of memory and completing every run within 277 seconds.
en.why: It demonstrates that competitive performance on complex selective pickup-and-delivery routing problems with heterogeneous fleets can be achieved using lightweight code restricted to standard Python libraries.
